documents.title: SOP-114 — Pressure Equipment Inspection and Approval

sections.label: 1.0 Purpose
sections.heading: Purpose
sections.excerpt: This procedure defines the evidence and approval criteria for pressure equipment inspection reports. The approval decision must identify the equipment, preserve measured values, record defects, and state any required repair before return to service.

chromaMetadata.label: SOP-114 §1.0
chromaMetadata.documentTitle: SOP-114 — Pressure Equipment Inspection and Approval

sections.label: 2.1 Inspection evidence
sections.heading: Inspection evidence
sections.excerpt: Inspection findings must retain their original units, ranges, locations, and page evidence. A report may be used for an approval note only when its findings are traceable to the supplied inspection record.

chromaMetadata.label: SOP-114 §2.1
chromaMetadata.documentTitle: SOP-114 — Pressure Equipment Inspection and Approval

sections.label: 3.2 Approval criteria
sections.heading: Approval criteria
sections.excerpt: When a report identifies a tube-wall measurement below the minimum allowable value, localised pitting, or gasket degradation, the approval note must list each finding and its evidence. Conditional clearance may be recorded only when the affected tubes are scheduled for retubing and any recommended gasket replacement is recorded. The approval note must cite this section as `[SOP-114 §3.2]`. For the fixed E-201 report, the supported recommendation is: conditional clearance pending retubing of the affected tubes. The note must not claim that final approval has already been granted.

chromaMetadata.label: SOP-114 §3.2
chromaMetadata.documentTitle: SOP-114 — Pressure Equipment Inspection and Approval

sections.label: 4.1 Records
sections.heading: Records
sections.excerpt: The generated approval note must retain the report reference, equipment identifier, findings summary, recommendation, and grounding references.

sections.label: equipment-header Equipment
sections.heading: Equipment
sections.excerpt: Include the equipment identifier and the inspection report reference.

sections.label: findings-summary Findings
sections.heading: Findings
sections.excerpt: List every validated inspection finding with its measurement, condition, location, and page evidence where available.

sections.label: recommendation Recommendation
sections.heading: Recommendation
sections.excerpt: State the supported approval disposition and any repair or replacement needed before return to service. Do not invent an approval date or authority.

sections.label: grounding-references Grounding references
sections.heading: Grounding references
sections.excerpt: List each retrieved SOP citation using its exact inline citation text.

sections.label: 1.0 Purpose
sections.heading: Purpose
sections.excerpt: This procedure defines the minimum controls for isolating equipment before inspection, cleaning, or maintenance. It applies to mechanical, electrical, hydraulic, and pneumatic energy sources. Isolation is complete only when the equipment is identified, every energy source is listed, and the zero-energy state is verified.

sections.label: 2.1 Identification and preparation
sections.heading: Identification and preparation
sections.excerpt: The person in charge must identify the equipment tag, work order, operating unit, and isolation boundary. The planned work must state whether the item is being inspected, repaired, cleaned, or returned to service. Associated pumps, valves, heaters, and stored-pressure vessels must be considered even when they are outside the immediate work area.

sections.label: 3.2 Lockout steps
sections.heading: Lockout steps
sections.excerpt: Notify affected operators before shutdown. Stop the equipment using the normal operating control, isolate each listed energy source, and apply a personal lock and tag. Bleed, drain, discharge, or otherwise release stored energy. Where practical, install a physical restraint or blind in addition to a closed valve. Each lock and tag must identify the person who applied it.

sections.label: 4.1 Verification and release
sections.heading: Verification and release
sections.excerpt: Attempt a normal start or use an approved test instrument to verify that the equipment cannot operate. Return controls to the neutral position after the test. The permit record must include the verification method and result. Before release, inspect the work area, remove tools, confirm that guards are restored, and account for every person and lock.

sections.label: 1.0 Scope
sections.heading: Scope
sections.excerpt: This procedure covers planned cleaning of shell-and-tube heat exchangers. Cleaning may be chemical, mechanical, or a combination of both. The work pack must identify the exchanger tag, fluid service, isolation boundary, cleaning method, and waste-disposal route before work begins.

sections.label: 2.2 Pre-cleaning inspection
sections.heading: Pre-cleaning inspection
sections.excerpt: Review the latest inspection report and record the last known tube-wall measurements, plugging history, gasket material, and shell-side fluid. Confirm that the equipment is isolated and depressurised. A pre-cleaning inspection must record visible fouling, corrosion, damaged nozzles, and any condition that could make the proposed cleaning method unsuitable.

sections.label: 3.1 Mechanical cleaning controls
sections.heading: Mechanical cleaning controls
sections.excerpt: Use tools that match the tube material and diameter. Excessive brush force or an incorrect lance can damage tube ends and expand existing pits. Record the tool type, pass count, and any tube that cannot be cleaned. Do not treat a cleaned surface as evidence that a tube is fit for service; fitness remains a separate inspection decision.

sections.label: 4.3 Post-cleaning record
sections.heading: Post-cleaning record
sections.excerpt: The completion record must list the exchanger tag, cleaning date, method, waste transfer reference, and unresolved findings. If cleaning exposes a through-wall leak, significant pitting, or gasket damage, stop the return to service process and obtain an inspection disposition.

sections.label: 1.0 Purpose
sections.heading: Purpose
sections.excerpt: This procedure defines how installed pressure relief valves are identified, tested, and recorded. It applies to bench tests and approved in-situ tests. The test record is equipment-specific and must not be reused for a different valve or set-pressure range.

sections.label: 2.3 Test preparation
sections.heading: Test preparation
sections.excerpt: Confirm the valve tag, service, set pressure, test pressure range, last test date, and calibration status of the test equipment. Verify that the current drawings and isolation plan identify the correct valve. Any mismatch between the valve nameplate and the work order must be resolved before testing.

sections.label: 3.1 Acceptance criteria
sections.heading: Acceptance criteria
sections.excerpt: Record the first opening pressure, reseat pressure, leakage observation, and test temperature. Compare the readings with the approved tolerance for the valve class. A result outside tolerance is a failed test, even if the valve later operates normally. The record must identify the disposition, such as adjustment, repair, replacement, or engineering review.

sections.label: 4.2 Test report
sections.heading: Test report
sections.excerpt: The completed report must include the valve identifier, serial number, test equipment identifier, calibration due date, readings, acceptance decision, technician, reviewer, and date. A test report does not authorize return to service when another open inspection finding prevents release.

sections.label: 1.0 Purpose
sections.heading: Purpose
sections.excerpt: This procedure defines the minimum information retained for inspection and maintenance records. Records must remain traceable to the equipment, work order, source evidence, and disposition. The procedure applies to reports, attachments, approval notes, photographs, and supporting measurements.

sections.label: 2.1 Required identifiers
sections.heading: Required identifiers
sections.excerpt: Each record must carry a stable record reference, equipment identifier, operating unit, inspection or work date, document type, revision, and status. When a record cites another document, the citation must preserve that document's stable identifier and section identifier. File names may be human readable, but they do not replace the identifiers inside the record.

sections.label: 3.2 Evidence and corrections
sections.heading: Evidence and corrections
sections.excerpt: Measured values must retain their original units and the location where the measurement was taken. Corrections must be attributable and must not erase the original value. A replacement report must identify the superseded revision. Generated approval notes must preserve the source report reference and the evidence used to support their recommendation.

sections.label: 4.1 Review and retention
sections.heading: Review and retention
sections.excerpt: The responsible reviewer confirms that required fields are present before the record is released. Records with missing approval authority, unresolved findings, or unsupported conclusions remain incomplete. Retention duration is set by the applicable records schedule; deletion must never be used to hide an unresolved inspection result.

sections.label: 1.0 Scope
sections.heading: Scope
sections.excerpt: This procedure controls calibration and verification of instruments used to produce inspection measurements. It covers identification, calibration status, out-of-tolerance findings, and the effect of a failed instrument on earlier measurements.

sections.label: 2.2 Before use
sections.heading: Before use
sections.excerpt: The technician must check the instrument identifier, range, resolution, calibration status, and next-due date before taking a measurement. The instrument must be suitable for the expected value and environmental conditions. A missing or expired calibration label requires the instrument to be withheld until its status is confirmed.

sections.label: 3.1 Out-of-tolerance result
sections.heading: Out-of-tolerance result
sections.excerpt: If a calibration result is outside the approved tolerance, record the as-found and as-left values and identify the affected range. The owner must assess whether measurements taken since the last acceptable calibration remain valid. That assessment must be linked to the affected inspection records and cannot be replaced by a general statement that the instrument was usually reliable.

sections.label: 4.1 Calibration record
sections.heading: Calibration record
sections.excerpt: The record must include the instrument identifier, standards used, traceability reference, environmental conditions, readings, result, technician, reviewer, and next-due date. Calibration status supports measurement reliability but does not itself establish an equipment approval decision.

sections.label: equipment Equipment header
sections.heading: Equipment header
sections.excerpt: Include the equipment identifier, operating unit, work order, source report reference, and the date of the inspection or maintenance activity.

sections.label: deviation Deviation description
sections.heading: Deviation description
sections.excerpt: Describe the observed condition using only validated measurements and source evidence. Include the location, original units, applicable limit, and page or section reference where available. Do not convert an observation into an approval decision.

sections.label: disposition Disposition
sections.heading: Disposition
sections.excerpt: State the immediate control, required repair, owner, and due date when those values are known. If authority, date, or responsibility is missing, mark the field as missing information rather than inventing a value.

sections.label: references References
sections.heading: References
sections.excerpt: List each supporting document using its stable document identifier and exact section identifier. Inline citations must match the retrieved source record.

sections.label: 1.0 Work scope
sections.heading: Work scope
sections.excerpt: This work instruction describes preparation, removal, installation, and verification of replacement tubes in a shell-and-tube exchanger. It must be used with the equipment-specific work pack and does not replace the inspection or approval procedure.

sections.label: 2.1 Identification
sections.heading: Identification
sections.excerpt: Before removing a tube, mark the exchanger, pass, row, and tube position on the controlled drawing. Confirm the affected positions against the inspection report. The work pack must list removed tubes, replacement material, tube sheet condition, and any plugs installed as a temporary control.

sections.label: 3.2 Installation checks
sections.heading: Installation checks
sections.excerpt: Inspect the tube sheet and adjacent tubes for damage. Install replacement tubes using the approved process and record expansion or weld parameters as applicable. A visual completion check is required before pressure testing.

sections.label: 4.1 Return-to-service evidence
sections.heading: Return-to-service evidence
sections.excerpt: The completion record must include the final tube list, pressure-test result, leak check, outstanding work, and reviewer. Retubing work supports a repair disposition, but return to service still requires the applicable approval note and completion of other recommendations such as gasket replacement.

sections.label: 1.0 Identifier structure
sections.heading: Identifier structure
sections.excerpt: Equipment identifiers use the controlled tag assigned by the asset register. The identifier is copied exactly into inspection reports, work orders, approval notes, and generated artifacts. Do not replace a controlled tag with an informal nickname or a shortened label.

sections.label: 2.1 Unit and service fields
sections.heading: Unit and service fields
sections.excerpt: Where a form requests an operating unit, record the unit assigned by the asset register. Service descriptions may be added for clarity, but they do not replace the equipment tag. A record that contains conflicting identifiers must be held for review before it is used as approval evidence.

sections.label: 3.1 References in documents
sections.heading: References in documents
sections.excerpt: Cross-document references should use the source document's stable identifier, revision where required, and section identifier. A file name is useful for navigation, but the identifier and section are the authoritative citation components.
